records.head: 96a5718f8e8b28a4e30af0211f2d7ab6ac1cf9bd
records.title: Match legacy JavaScript MIME types exactly in HTML inventories (R3.13)
records.body:
## Problem

The HTML script scanner accepts any suffix beginning with `1` after eight JavaScript MIME types. For example, `text/javascript1evil` and `application/javascript1.0` become executable scripts in the inventory even though browsers treat them as data. Inline blocks then contribute false application endpoints, and external blocks create false page imports and execution roles.

## Change

Match the six legacy types `text/javascript1.0` through `text/javascript1.5` exactly. The other standard JavaScript MIME types retain exact, ASCII case-insensitive matching.

The existing module, Babel/JSX, empty-type and MIME-parameter policies remain. Unsupported types still consume their whole script block, so the next real script keeps its byte range and line. Application tests also retain facts from an explicitly supplied standalone data.js file while removing its false page import.

The exact legacy list follows [WHATWG MIME Sniffing §4.6](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type). This change does not expand into the scanner's intentional Babel/JSX or parameter handling.

Roadmap: R3.13. Public claim `2226d2e` preceded implementation; the branch is based on upstream `7116cc6`.

## Validation

- Original source: **6 regression failures and 4 passing controls** across the public scanner and application graph.
- All **10 new regression groups** pass. The complete JavaScript and analysis suites pass: **250 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**, across 31 test targets including doc-test targets.
- Real Chromium **158.0.8127.18** executes 16 standard JavaScript MIME fixtures and leaves ten unsupported suffix fixtures inert. Original scanner: 26 scripts, including all ten false positives. Fixed scanner: exactly the same 16 scripts Chromium executed.
- Strict all-target Clippy, workspace formatting, layer/lock checks, secret scanning, all L0–L2 WebAssembly gates and an unchanged source tree pass with Rust 1.99.
- The first full run caught a test-fixture expectation of `renderer` where the existing ordinary-web contract is `page`. Only that test name and role assertion were corrected; product code was unchanged. The failed run remains available.

[Original Chromium comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43036021283/job/130574918129) · [Complete fixed validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43038199945/job/130582606184) · [Initial fixture diagnostic](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43037534160/job/130580258150)

The complete suite validates `065ee639`. Final head `96a5718f` changes only ROADMAP and STATUS; a separate fixed-head check verifies every implementation, test and dependency file is identical, and repeats formatting, secret scanning and diff checks.

[Final documentation and identity check](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43038999162/job/130585447800)

records.head: ed087f661d3e5766d8806f095b0d8548d9a09fda
records.title: Preserve literal values in JavaScript structural fingerprints (R3.12)
records.body:
## Problem

The structural fingerprint records literal node kinds but omits BigInt values, regular-expression patterns and flags, and template text. Programs with different results can consequently share a fingerprint. Application comparisons pair different files as structural renames, and bundle comparisons omit these literal changes from their changed-module inventory.

## Change

Include the exact parsed BigInt value, the regular-expression pattern and flag set, and each template element's raw text. Tags can observe raw escapes, including escapes with no cooked value. New variable-length payloads have a byte-length prefix.

Equivalent BigInt spellings and regular-expression flag orders still match. Identifier renaming and the existing string, number, boolean and operator behavior remain intact.

Fingerprints of programs containing these literals change. Saved older inventories still hold the older fingerprints; reanalyze both sides with the updated analyzer to use the corrected comparison.

Roadmap: R3.12. Public claim `dfd752af` preceded implementation. The branch is independently based on `22c44d01`.

## Validation

- Original source on the current base: **6 regression failures, 5 passing controls**. All **11 public regression groups** pass with the fix.
- Complete JavaScript and analysis suites: **254 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**, across 32 targets including doc tests.
- Actual Node **22.23.4** execution of 14 hand-written program pairs: nine distinct runtime results and five equivalent controls. Original fingerprints hide all nine differences; fixed fingerprints distinguish all nine and report each changed webpack module, while all five equivalent pairs remain matched.
- The runtime comparison covers large BigInts beyond floating-point integer precision, regex patterns and flags, template prefixes and tails, tagged raw escapes and invalid cooked escapes.
- Strict all-target Clippy, workspace formatting, layer/lock checks, secret scanning, all L0–L2 WebAssembly checks and an unchanged source tree pass with Rust 1.99.

[Original Node comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43039360696/job/130586691737) · [Full fixed validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43040559888/job/130590896107)

The initial runtime probe used `7116cc6`; the fingerprint and comparison implementations are unchanged in `22c44d01`, whose intervening change concerns source-map inventories. The regression negative controls and complete quality gates ran on the new base with tested head `b6864b6e`.

Final head `ed087f66` changes only ROADMAP and STATUS. A separate fixed-head check verifies every implementation, test and dependency file is identical to the fully tested head, then repeats formatting, secret scanning and diff checks.

[Final documentation and identity check](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43041790806/job/130595207200)
